decisive_items: progressive unilateral skin hardening on his right thigh and buttock for 7 years
ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks with loss of skin elasticity
subtle increase in density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment but no evidence of inflammation
response.rationale: The unilateral stony-hard plaque with hyperpigmentation, loss of elasticity, and deep dermal sclerosis with adipocyte entrapment and absent inflammation is most consistent with morphea. Fibroblastic rheumatism is the runner-up because it shares CD34 expression and skin/joint involvement, but it lacks the required nodules and polyarthritis; NSF is excluded by normal blood tests and no renal disease.

rejected.why: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis requires renal insufficiency/gadolinium exposure; normal routine blood tests, childhood onset, unilateral involvement, and negative Alcian blue are incompatible.
